ai.summary: Modified `processedPathKey` in `scripts/update-stripe-subscriptions.ts` to use raw `customerId` instead of prefixed `cust_${customerId}`. Formatting adjusted for arrow functions and console logs. Internal tooling change only.

eli5.text: The internal system that updates customer subscriptions was changed so it now uses the customer's ID directly instead of adding a prefix to it when tracking which accounts have already been processed. This only affects how the company's back-end tools keep track of work behind the scenes; there's nothing visible to customers. The change was deployed on April 18, 2025, and is part of routine maintenance, not a new feature.

ai.title: Add sendToRelaceLongContext for large file requests
ai.summary: Added `sendToRelaceLongContext` in `backend/src/llm-apis/relace-api.ts` to POST large file edits to Relace's long context endpoint. `backend/src/process-file-block.ts` now triggers this request asynchronously for files between `LARGE_FILE_TOKEN_LIMIT` and 64k tokens, while continuing the standard `handleLargeFile` flow. Includes 100s timeout and error logging.

eli5.text: Files in the middle size range (between roughly 'large' and 64,000 tokens) now get an extra behind-the-scenes request sent to Relace's long-context processing path, while the usual flow continues. When you edit one of these files, the system asynchronously pushes the edit over to a specialized endpoint designed for bigger jobs, giving it up to 100 seconds and logging any errors if it fails. To you, nothing changes at the surface: you still submit edits the same way and get the same results, only now some files quietly get additional processing support on the backend. This is live today for the affected size range.

ai.title: Initial credit grants expire via getNextQuotaReset
ai.summary: Auth flow now passes `getNextQuotaReset` expiry to `createInitialCreditGrant`. Prevents free grants from persisting indefinitely for new signups. Affects `web/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/auth-options.ts`. `knowledge.md` codifies single-source-of-truth rule for derived quota dates.

eli5.text: When someone signs up for a new account, they are given a small amount of free usage credits, and those credits now automatically expire after a set period instead of lasting forever. The expiration date is calculated using the same method the system already uses to reset regular usage limits, so the free credits follow the same schedule as paid ones. If you signed up for a new account recently, your free credits will now disappear after the reset period, and if you looked at your account balance, you would see a clear expiration date attached to those credits.

ai.title: codebuff.json startup processes auto-run on CLI launch
ai.summary: New `codebuff.json` config file enables auto-starting background dev processes when Freebuff launches. `npm-app/src/index.ts` calls `loadCodebuffConfig` and `startDevProcesses` before project init; `npm-app/src/json-config/parser.ts` validates against a Zod schema (`CodebuffConfigSchema`), `dev-process-manager.ts` spawns commands via `runBackgroundCommand`. Scope: CLI only (`npm-app`); `.codebuffignore` excludes `codebuff.json` from context. `runBackgroundCommand` now takes a `mode: 'user' | 'assistant'` param, suppressing green log output for user-initiated processes.

eli5.text: When you open the tool for a project, it now checks for a codebuff.json file and can automatically start background tasks like a web server, so you don't have to run them yourself before getting started. This works through a new settings file that lists which processes to kick off, and the tool will validate the format before launching them. Anything in that file is kept out of the project's searchable content, and the background tasks are labeled differently so user-started processes stay quieter. This is live today and works whenever you launch the tool with that config file present.

ai.title: Enforce .gitignore during file writes
ai.summary: New `isFileIgnored` helper in `common/src/project-file-tree.ts` checks files against `DEFAULT_IGNORED_FILES` and directory-specific `.gitignore` patterns. `applyChanges` in `common/src/util/changes.ts` now skips writes to ignored files, returning an `ignored` array. `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts` reports failures for ignored files, preventing writes to paths excluded by `.gitignore` or `.codebuffignore`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to write or edit a file that your project's.gitignore or.codebuffignore file excludes, it no longer silently writes to it. Instead, it skips that file and reports a clear message that it could not write because the file is ignored, so files you intentionally hide from version control are no longer accidentally updated by the assistant.

ai.title: Experimental Gemini thinking mode and stopSequences support
ai.summary: Added experimental mode support for Gemini thinking via `getThinkingStream` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Unified `stopSequences` parameter across Claude, Gemini, and OpenAI API clients in `backend/src/llm-apis/`. Updated `common/src/constants.ts` and `npm-app/src/utils/tool-renderers.ts` to handle new tool call formats and thinking output. Gemini fallback logic simplified to use `gemini-2.5-pro-preview` directly.

eli5.text: The assistant can now think through responses in a step-by-step way when using Gemini, a newer model provider, similar to how a person might pause to organize their thoughts before answering. It also now accepts the same set of stop commands (like specific phrases that end a response) across different AI systems, making behavior more consistent. You wouldn't see a dramatic difference unless you're using advanced settings that rely on these features, but the system is now more unified behind the scenes. This is now live and part of the core system as of April 2025.

ai.title: Start updateCodebuff before dev processes in index.ts
ai.summary: In npm-app/src/index.ts, `updateCodebuff()` is invoked before `startDevProcesses()`. This ensures the update process begins immediately, rather than waiting for config loading and startup processes to complete. The change affects the CLI startup sequence, potentially reducing time-to-ready for projects with heavy startup configurations.

eli5.text: When the command-line tool starts, it now begins checking for updates earlier, before it finishes loading project settings and starting background tasks. If you launch a project that takes a while to configure, you may see the update check happen sooner instead of waiting for everything else to load first. The change affects only the order of operations during startup and does not add or remove any features.
